speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are presenting with a chronic cough and recurrent bouts of bronchitis. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present, and do they occur more frequently in specific seasons or environments?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very long duration for chronic bronchitis symptoms, especially without a smoking history. Given the copious thick, yellow-green sputum and morning predominance, have you ever been diagnosed with bronchiectasis or cystic fibrosis, or do you experience hemoptysis?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. The combination of an 11-year history of chronic cough with copious purulent sputum, morning predominance, and recurrent "bronchitis" in a non-smoker is classic for this condition, often requiring confirmation with a high-resolution CT scan to visualize bronchial dilation.
